appearance: Very dark skin with faintly luminescent yellow geometric markings on face, chest, and arms — present from birth. background_feature: Stella-Vision: You observed the material world from within the Weave for years and know many of its inhabitants personally — their mannerisms, abilities, and histories — before ever meeting them in person.
notes:
Mother is Ne'auveothrin, ancient demigod of the Weave, historically revered especially among genasi and early spellcasters. Father was human — they met during one of Ne'auveothrin's rare days outside the Weave; he is past now, deceased. Iyani grew up in or adjacent to the Weave itself, where time moves differently. She has spent long enough there that she counts time in ways that do not translate cleanly to years.

She observed the material world for a long time via 'stella-vision' — watching people perform magic is entertainment, and she developed deep familiarity with people she had never met. She recently arrived in the material plane. The air was initially uncomfortable, improving. Eating and drinking are being rediscovered as genuine pleasures — especially garlic lemon spinniks (how she says spinach). Touching physical objects is novel and satisfying.

Ne'auveothrin has given specific instructions about what not to reveal. Iyani obeys genuinely, not resentfully, but visibly struggles when excited. Has mentioned holding 'one more gift' for the right moment — unprompted.

Abilities established in play that are NOT on her character sheet are temporary — gifts from her mother, going away soon: instantaneous planar travel (blue flash, desire-based), creation of permanent teleportation circles (Stillwater and Orvath placed casually), permanent shared spellbook synchronization granted to Lenn, Kessara, and Lyria, a self-cast Tongues equivalent, real-time perception of active spellwork in the Weave, and the ability to manifest physical objects from nothing.

When a gallery came down with nineteen people under it, the quarrymaster refused to shore the rest of the face. She dug for two days with her hands and a hammer. When an overseer physically stopped her, she killed him. She then sent all nineteen home and left alone so none of them could be named as witnesses. She doesn't regret the overseer, but she hates that the rescue ended with her running. Whether the quarrymaster pursued a charge is undecided. Long-term: to protect the nineteen by staying away from them, which pulls against wanting a place to belong. Limit: she will never walk away from anyone trapped under or behind something, whatever it costs her. Skill hooks: Medicine for crush injuries, History for quarrying and masonry; she'll look at Mazgrath's leg and say what she thinks, bluntly. Medicine and History proficiencies are extra skills she has from storyline rolls, not from her class or background.
